analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied source against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. provider-plan.yml head:183-185 removes the size-required marker from provider/cluster builds and release checks; head:163-168 documents that these lanes can now use Sandbox runners with the approval's pinned size when job shapes are off. Job-selection predicates, explicit shape values, fallback labels and workflow permissions are unchanged. provider-tests.yml changes only comments (head:56-58, 862-864); its visible base source shows routed builds uploading test products for downstream shards (122-127, 201-206, 289-294) and saving caches only under existing event/ref conditions (36-39). No observed authorization bypass, plaintext disclosure, signing-policy change or skipped security gate is established here. CI build caches are not the inference prefix cache governed by T-041.
Integration must examine darkbloom-route.yml's interpretation of the removed marker and approval/fallback enforcement, together with the build/product and release-cache actions. Moving product-producing and cache-writing jobs onto this runner path makes runner isolation, artifact provenance and cache integrity material to A-011/A-017, T-013 and T-054. The supplied evidence does not establish that Sandbox hosts are adversarial, that isolation is missing, or that these products become qualified release artifacts, so none is asserted as a regression. Likewise, smaller approved sizes could cause resource failures, but comments alone do not establish an unsafe approval or fail-open gate. Remaining uncertainty is whether the expanded routing preserves the build trust and failure contracts; resolve it in the combined review rather than treating absent implementations as missing controls. Runtime encryption, attestation, billing, privileged helpers and inference admission are not changed by the supplied hunks.
